newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah softens on ample supply.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah softens on ample supply.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah softened against the dollar in moderate late trading on Thursday on the back of ample liquidity, dealers said.
One European bank dealer said liquidity seemed to be the main cause for the weakening of the rupiah although it failed to break the strong resistance level at the 2,430.0 level.
Spot trading ranged between 2,428.0 and 2,430.0 on Thursday, with more rupiah softening seen in the afternoon.
Spot rupiah was at 2,429.25/29.75 at 0845 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,429.0/30.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,429.0/29.5 and 2,428.5/29.0, respectively.
Overnight rupiah fell to two percent from 8.5 percent in the morning. Overnight swap closed at 0.15/0.20 and tom/next swaps were last at 0.15/0.20 points.
"Sentiment on the rupiah wasn't bad but a flushed market appears to cause some dollar purchases," the dealer said.
Dealers said longer-term swaps continued to increase as offshore operators went long on the rupiah in forwards.

"I don't know whether it's due to returning confidence after the election or due to the Thai factor," the European bank dealer said, adding that a relatively smooth election seemed to encourage operators to return to the market.
The Thai central bank had asked operators to stop quoting tom/next to offshore players to close their funding sources.
Dealers said the Thai problem continued to hang over the Jakarta forward market, driving longer-term forward rates to increase each time offshore players were squeezed over there.
"Our forward market is a bit in disorder because of the Thai factor. Offshore players fear a similar move in Jakarta despite a denial by Bank Indonesia," another bank dealer said.
She said offshore players were going long in forwards to factor in possible risks.
Buying interest in the forward market sustained although further uptrend was limited by ample short-term funds.
One-month swaps edged up to 12.5/13.0 from 11.5/12.5, two to 26.00/27.75 from 24.0/27.0, three to 37.00/38.75 from 37.0/39.0 and six to 77.5/79.0 from 76.0/78.0 points.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,418/2,610 and its conversion band at 2,418/2,466 on Thursday.

Dealers said another impending issue was whether the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) would accept the election outcome. PPP leaders were meeting on Thursday and said they would issue a statement on Friday.
